headline: Graph-structured biological priors linked to disease outcomes in biobank-scale data
label: Biologically Informed Graph Models
summary: Biobank-scale cohorts now let structured representations be tested against disease-level association outputs across modalities.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of structured representations of biobank-scale data to link measurements to disease outcomes. Graph in Graph (GiG) encodes biological structure directly, modeling person-phenotype and per-patient omics signaling graphs to predict type 2 diabetes. PUMA takes an unsupervised route, splitting over 1,000 phenotypes in 150,000 Lifelines individuals into seven aging dimensions linked to future disease. A self-supervised VICReg study on UK Biobank abdominal MRI links learned features to 158 of 562 diseases, including MASH. A transcript-aware rare-variant framework refines gene-based association tests, with simulations reporting calibrated false-positive rates and competitive power. The other items pursue the goal through different representations rather than explicit graph priors. What is new is the combination of graph-structured biological priors with disease-level association outputs.
